Linus: Quick note — observed a regional divergence in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout (canary id c-20260317-9). EU hit-rate down ~18% vs NA at similar traffic mix. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/cache/prefix-hit-rate
Maria G: Thanks Linus. Any correlation with batching changes or cache keying tweak from the rollout?
Linus: Early signal points to keying + kernel path interaction. We changed the cache fingerprint to include `quant_profile` for safety, but the kernel selector also routes short-seq requests to the new fast-kernel which strips some prefix metadata in the serialized KV key (probable collision).
AJ: Can you paste the sample key before/after?
Linus: Sure — pasted from sampled keys (sanitized):
```
# BEFORE
model:v2|route:chat|prompt_hash:0x7a3f|quant:q8_0
# AFTER
model:v2|route:chat|prompt_hash:0x7a3f
```
Looks like `quant` ended up not being serialized consistently for fast-kernel path, so keys de-duplicated across quant profiles causing low effective hit-rate in EU (where q8_0 is more common).
Sophia: Oof. That would explain a lot. EU traffic has higher q8_0 usage because dedicated pools prefer that config. NA uses q4_0 more.
Maria G: Any perf regressions from adding the `quant` to the key previously? We added it to avoid wrong-cache-serving across quant variants.
Linus: No perf cost, just the inconsistency across codepaths. The fast-kernel path has a small serialization shortcut to reduce allocation; missed `quant` field.
AJ: What's the immediate mitigation? Patch kernel to always include `quant` in key serialization (hotfix), or change routing to prefer NA-style kernel until patched?
Linus: Hotfix queued as PR: r/eng-runtime#3241. I'll push a patch that restores deterministic serialization for KV key. Rolling a canary to EU 1 region first.
deploy-bot: deploy started r/eng-runtime#3241 -> canary eu-1 at 2026-03-18T14:22:10Z.
Maria G: Also propose a short-term routing policy tweak: prefer kernel-stable for regions with >10% q8_0 traffic until canary completes. We can flip it with config flag `regional_kernel_affinity`.
AJ: Good. Can we also run a synthetic warmup job to repopulate prefix entries after the fix? Cold-region artifacts might persist because replication lag is ~30s and many keys were overwritten.
Sophia: I'll run a targeted prefetch sweep for top 5k prefixes in EU using the prewarm tool (job id prewarm-20260318-02). It will use authenticated sampling to avoid user data leakage.
Linus: Thanks. Action items: (1) Linus push hotfix + canary (in progress), (2) Maria G toggle regional_kernel_affinity for EU -> stable kernel, (3) Sophia run prewarm job, (4) AJ run post-fix profiling for KV serialization/p99 to ensure no regressions.
AJ: I'll capture flamegraphs + `kv-serialize` timing before/after and post results here. Expected window for full recovery ~10-15 minutes post-deploy + prewarm.
Maria G: Also we should add a unit test that validates key serialization across both kernel codepaths — create one in `runtime/kv/tests` and add to CI.
Linus: On it. I'll assign test + PR dependency.
deploy-bot: canary passed for eu-1 at 2026-03-18T14:28:05Z. No increase in error-rate.
Sophia: Prewarm job started. Rough ETA 8min for top-5k prefixes.
AJ: First profiling snapshot attached (summary): p50 serialize 120us -> 125us after fix, p99 580us -> 600us. negligible. Will upload detailed traces once the sweep finishes.
Maria G: Great. Retrospect: we should add a lint around KV key assembly to prevent future divergence when adding fields. Also add metrics for key-entropy to detect sudden drops.
Linus: Agreed. Closing loop: will follow up with a short postmortem note if any residual gap remains after 30m. Thanks team :thumbsup:
